title: 2001 HMMT February Team Problem 5
statement: Find all \(x\) between \(-\frac{\pi}{2}\) and \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) such that \(1-\sin ^{4} x-\cos ^{2} x=\frac{1}{16}\).

solutions.text: \(1-\sin ^{4} x-\cos ^{2} x \stackrel{1}{16} \Rightarrow\left(16-16 \cos ^{2} x\right)-\sin ^{4} x-1=0 \Rightarrow 16 \sin ^{4} x-\) \(16 \sin ^{2} x+1=0\). Use the quadratic formula in \(\sin x\) to obtain \(\sin ^{2} x=\frac{1}{2} \pm \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\). Since \(\cos 2 x=1-2 \sin ^{2} x= \pm \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), we get \(x= \pm \frac{\pi}{12}, \pm \frac{5 \pi}{12}\).
